solar.data_origin: Approximate SILSO sunspot number v2 cycle table, cycles 1-25 (dates of the minima and maxima of the 13-month smoothed series and the maximum values, rounded; cycle 25's maximum provisional), entered by hand and not verified against the SILSO files: check before quantitative use. The monthly values are synthesised from it with noise; they are not observations.

forcing_export.note: annual means: the record, then the forecast median (TSI) and the median of the members' energy balance (surface)

limitations: the sunspot record is synthesised from a cycle table unless a monthly record is given; synthetic months carry noise, not observations
single smooth curves per cycle: no double peaks, no hemispheric asymmetry; forecasts of cycles not yet started are climatology with a weak AR(1) memory (no polar-field precursor)
irradiance, UV, ozone and UV index follow linear proxies of the sunspot number; the UV variability differs by about a factor of two between instruments and reconstructions
flares are a stochastic rate model: the counts and the largest flares of the record are synthetic draws, not a flare list
the climate response is a two-layer global energy balance without the stratospheric (top-down) or ocean-dynamics pathways that observations suggest may amplify it
the disk shows an illustrative day: region positions, sizes and flares are random draws consistent with the cycle, not solar observations

targets.source: Holocene statistics from 14C (Usoskin, Solanki & Kovaltsov 2007, rounded)

epochs.evidence: 14C and 10Be in tree rings and ice (e.g. Usoskin et al. 2007)
epochs.name: Oort Minimum

epochs.evidence: 14C (Eddy 1976); naked-eye sunspots and aurorae in East Asian chronicles
epochs.name: Medieval Maximum

epochs.evidence: 14C and 10Be (Eddy 1976 named it after G. Spörer); the isotope records suggest an earlier start around 1400
epochs.name: Spörer Minimum

epochs.evidence: telescopic observations (very few spots, mostly in the southern hemisphere), rare aurorae, high 14C and 10Be (Eddy 1976; Usoskin et al. 2015)
epochs.name: Maunder Minimum

epochs.evidence: telescopic: weak SILSO cycles 5 and 6 (not a grand minimum by the decadal definition)
epochs.name: Dalton Minimum

limitations: before the cycle table the cycles are synthesised around a catalogue of epochs (a summary of the literature, not a reconstruction): their dates and amplitudes are illustrative
the slow brightening of the quiet Sun is uncertain: low, central and high TSI scenarios span it
the cosmogenic production is a calibrated proxy, not cosmic-ray transport; no geomagnetic-field change
volcanic and CO2 forcings are rounded comparison forcings; no aerosols besides volcanoes, no land use, no orbital forcing
the regional winter response is an illustrative parametrisation of the top-down pathway, not a circulation model
the dynamo map is a conceptual model calibrated to grand-minimum statistics; it makes grand maxima too short and too rare
